questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted something within Europe to be able to finans my study abroad. 
I wanted somewhere with a different culture and different nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved studying abroad in Portugal! It is a very great country to spent a semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I did not have a lot of issues with the information needed prior to my arrival. 
There was some confusion about classes and if my credits could transfer. 
They posted the classes for the semester late, so I had trouble checking the classes and so on until very close to my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: NOVA hosted a welcome week where they introduced us to the basics we needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
We had trouble with the OLA. NOVA did not have access to the official website to sign it, and there was a lot of back and forth to get it signed the proper way. This was a little exhausting, however all the staff we talked to in person were all very helpful. 
The exam schedeule and the schedeule for midterms should be posted before the semester starts at NOVA, I would recommend to check these before planning any trips - as most midterms and finals are obligatory.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing already in February. I got the apartment recommended by someone who knew someone who had stayed there. The housing situation in Lisbon is worse than in Copenhagen. I would recommend to double check the status of the apartment before moving in. Contact students who have been to Lisbon in earlier semesters and get their recommendations. Check facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living off campus in Lisbon. Campus is quite far away from the city, so it is best to live close to either cais do sodre, santos, alcantara mar og belem. The train goes directly from these stations to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy and simple to enroll in classes. The first round of signups for classes lasted a few days and you had time to check which one to choose, after that you were assigned. I was lucky to get assigned all but one of the classes I had wished for. For the second round it was "first come first served" which was a bit stressful. However the process at NOVA seemed easier than the process from other destinations.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: See comment above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think they had an email you could contact, however I did not need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all classes but one - which luckily were all the obligatory ones, then I just had to choose an elective in the second round. 
I got Economic History, Micro 3 and Public Economics transferred as obligatory classes in Denmark, which was great.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the excel sheet with classes at KU that has previously been accepted. Search for information on the schools website and make a groupchat with other people going to the same destination - they might have found documents that you haven't:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was positively surprised about the academics at NOVA.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some of the courses were easier than the ones at KU and some were the same level. 
I think the biggest difficulty is to understand the different learning methods used at NOVA. 
Overall the academic burden was smaller than what I am used to - but this might be due to the fact that all my classes were pass/fail based and that I had much more time (no student job).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
We were taught in much smaller classrooms with fewer students resulting in a more intimate classroom. 
We both had practical and theoretical classes, however I found that they seemed less different than in KU. We did not have time to solve assignments and so on in the practical classes, it was mostly the teacher solving exercises as a lecture. 
Public economics and Advanced Microeconomics were similar to the teaching style at KU for the Economics Bachelor. 
Other classes were more discussion based and way more empirical than theoretical, which in my opinion was a nice change.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Microeconomics (7 ECTS)
Public Economics (7 ECTS)
Economic History (3,5 ECTS)
Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History (3,5 ECTS)
Seminar in European Economics (7 ECTS)
Law in Business and Economics (3,5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Seminar in European Economics !!! This was by far my favorite class. The class was discussion based, and the professor was really good. It was nice to experience a more empirical approach to teaching and learn how to apply economic theory to the world. You do have to write a free assignment over the time of the course, however I did not find the workload to be too bad, as long as you start in advance. Make sure to be in a group with people with the same ambition level as you. The workload was probably equivalent to one of the assignments in "Økonomi i samfundet".

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
To get the Navigante card you need to pay some fees.
All the Erasmus events cost money. 
Many cafés and restaurants in Lisbon are very turist oriented, so the prices were higher than I expected, however everything is still cheaper in Lisbon than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee at the local cafés is only around 1-2 euro.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
NOVA had everything. Surf, Yoga, festivals, tennis etc.
I was very impressed about the offers that NOVA had. There were a lot of different clubs like the surf club, sports club, student union (arranging parties etc), mindspace, several consulting clubs, green club and many others.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I recommend attending the events hosted by Mindspace.
I joined the HR-team in the club and this was a great way to meet other students from other nationalities. You do not need to join the club to join the activities. They host yoga, mindfulness, two retreats a semester and many creative activities. If you check their instagram they have a link to join a whatsapp and you will get the scheduele for the yoga, pilates and mindfulness classes. The classes are only around 3-5€ and are on campus.
Surf!! There is a club at the uni, where you can rent a surfboard if you already now how to surf. If you are new to surf I would recommend to head down the other end of the beach to "Lisbon Surf Camp" (
https://www.lisbonsurfcamp.com/
). Here you can get a membership where they offer 4 lessons a month and 8 rentals for 50€ (in 2025). I joined this club and loved it. It was the perfect way to fill the hours between classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the country!! Madeira!!!, Ericeira!!, Porto, South Coast, Serra de Estrella.
Check out
https://nazarewaves.com/
and head to Nazare to see the biggest waves of the world when they put out warnings!! This was one of my top experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: This was pretty easy. Portugal is an easy country to be a guest. People are friendly and helpfull - much more than the Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest cultural challenges was that the public transportation is unreliable and that in Portugal things are less organized - "you can't control the sea, but you can learn how to surf" is the mantra.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laissez-faire and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Double check the housing situation - you might not get the perfect place, but remember that it is only for a short amount of time. Do not let it scare you away from going abroad, but be aware of the fact that it is difficult to find good housing, and that you might need to make compromises. 
2. Make sure to plan you trips early - time is going to run by so fast, and you should make sure to take advantage of the ability to explore the beautiful country.
3. Remember to bring a good rain jacket and a warm sweater + sweats to wear inside. Portugal is great and sunny most of the year. However in the winter it gets surprisingly cold out of nowhere. The houses are not built for bad weather and are difficult to warm up resulting in the need for big sweaters indoor during winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I loved my semester abroad. I loved exploring a new country and making the most of the different daily-life by using the outdoors way more than I do back home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the homesickness - missing my family and friends back home. However did this not outweigh all the great great things I experienced!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
